brief: UBS's Daily Asia note argues the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% should not derail the equity rally, because most of the tightening is already priced: markets had braced for nearly four hikes this cycle versus UBS's forecast of two, and UBS still expects only one further 25bp move this year. Economic strength offsets the hawkish dot plot (16 of 18 officials now see another hike, up from half in June): the Fed raised 2026-27 growth forecasts, cut projected unemployment, and August retail sales beat expectations. UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027, arguing a harder environment would need higher yields, weaker earnings, and wider credit spreads together, not just one. UBS stays positioned for further equity gains while recommending diversification away from rate-sensitive, single-driver exposure. Separately, UBS expects the Bank of England to hold its rate at 3.75% through year-end despite UK inflation ticking up to 3.1%, and argues reported Japanese defense-spending increases would not materially worsen Japan's fiscal position, attributing the recent JGB yield rise to global yields and Bank of Japan tightening expectations rather than the defense headlines.
